On Wed, Sep 16, 2026 at 11:03 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Olivia — thanks for the context and the workload dump.

Quick thoughts from an implementation POV (summary before kickoff):

- Quantization: for a 7B dense model I'd prepare three candidate profiles:
  * QP-A: int8 dynamic — minimal quality delta, ~15–25% latency improvement
  * QP-B: 4-bit hybrid (select layers FP16) — larger latency/cost wins, needs small eval set (50 prompts)
  * QP-C: aggressive 4-bit full — biggest cost win, higher regression risk, use as fallback for batch jobs only

- KV/Prefix caching: enable prefix-level KV caching for chat sessions with TTL 24h; use a small LRU cache sized to 10k entries for early tests. Expect 12–18% token savings if 15% prefix reuse holds.

- Batching: implement adaptive batching with a 20ms max delay slab for chat and a 200ms slab for bulk embedding workers. This preserves p95 for chat while giving batch jobs throughput.

- Routing policy: suggested policy rules:
  1) If request.type == "chat" -> route to low-latency pool (QP-A or FP16)
  2) If request.tag == "batch" && latency_tolerance >= 500ms -> route to QP-C pool
  3) Fallback to FP16 on cache-miss spikes or if p95 > SLO for 5m window

I can pre-create these three model variants in your Dedicated test pool before the call; we'll run small AB runs and push results into the mutual action plan.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Token volume: ~10k tokens/day initially (we'll scale).

We will prioritize latency for chat — so route chat to the low-latency pool and only use aggressive QP-C for bulk nightly jobs. Also attaching our SOC2 questionnaire that the security/audit team may review during the kickoff.
